questions.question: Which other names are used for the procurement process?

options.A: "Order to cash" or the fulfillment process
options.B: "Plan to produce" or the production process
options.C: "Record to report" or the closing process
options.D: "Procure to pay", "P2P" or the sourcing process

questions.explanation: Procurement is concerned with acquiring (purchasing) materials and services.

questions.question: What is the first step of the simple procurement process?

options.A: Creating a purchase order
options.B: Creating a purchase requisition
options.C: Recording a goods receipt
options.D: Verifying the vendor invoice

questions.explanation: Order: requisition, purchase order, goods receipt, invoice verification, vendor payment.

questions.question: What is a purchase requisition?

options.A: An approval sent to the vendor that is a binding commitment to purchase
options.B: A document that verifies the materials received match the order
options.C: A request from the vendor for payment of the delivered materials
options.D: An internal "request to buy" needed materials, with materials, quantities and desired receipt date

questions.explanation: It can be generated automatically by fulfillment, production or material planning, or created manually.

questions.question: Which processes can automatically generate purchase requisitions?

options.A: Fulfillment, production and material planning
options.B: Financial accounting and overhead management only
options.C: Vendor payment and invoice verification
options.D: Period closing and settlement

questions.explanation: It can also be created manually by the user.

questions.question: What is a purchase order?

options.A: An internal request to buy materials that contains only quantities and dates
options.B: A record that verifies received materials match the specified order
options.C: An approval to purchase the requested materials, typically created by converting purchase requisitions, including pricing and terms
options.D: A document sent by the vendor requesting payment

questions.explanation: When sent to a vendor, it becomes a binding commitment to purchase under the stated terms.

questions.question: What is sending a purchase order to a vendor called, and sending it to another plant of the enterprise?

options.A: External procurement; internal procurement
options.B: Internal procurement; external procurement
options.C: Both are called external procurement
options.D: Direct procurement; indirect procurement

questions.explanation: Purchase orders can be sent to a vendor or to another plant within the enterprise.

questions.question: Which tasks does the ERP system perform automatically at goods receipt?

options.A: Updates the vendor master and creates the purchase requisition
options.B: Creates the vendor invoice and authorizes the payment
options.C: Updates G/L accounts, updates inventory quantity and value in the material master, and creates FI, CO and material documents as needed
options.D: Calculates the cost of goods manufactured and settles the order

questions.explanation: The goods receipt verifies the received materials match the purchase order.

questions.question: What is a three-way match in invoice verification?

options.A: Comparing the purchase requisition, the purchase order and the payment
options.B: Comparing the invoice, the payment and the bank statement
options.C: Comparing three different vendors for the same purchase order
options.D: Comparing the data in the purchase order, the goods receipt document and the invoice

questions.explanation: A two-way match compares only the invoice and purchase order.

questions.question: How does the system calculate the vendor payment amount when it authorizes a payment?

options.A: Based on the amount on the goods receipt only
options.B: Based on the terms specified in the purchase order
options.C: Based on the tolerance group of the employee
options.D: Based on the moving average price of the material

questions.explanation: Payments can be sent by electronic funds transfer or a printed check.

questions.question: Which three steps of the procurement process have a financial accounting consequence?

options.A: Goods receipt, invoice verification and vendor payment
options.B: Purchase requisition, purchase order and goods receipt
options.C: Purchase requisition, invoice verification and vendor payment
options.D: Purchase order, goods receipt and invoice verification

questions.explanation: Requisitions and purchase orders do not post to the general ledger.

topics.topicName: Enterprise structure: plant, valuation level, purchasing organization & storage location

questions.question: Which enterprise structure elements are involved in the procurement process?

options.A: Client, sales organization, distribution channel, division and shipping point
options.B: Company code, plant, material valuation level, purchasing organization, purchasing group and storage location
options.C: Controlling area, cost center, profit center and internal order
options.D: Chart of accounts, fiscal year variant, posting key and document type

questions.explanation: These elements define where procurement tasks are completed.

questions.question: What does a plant represent in an ERP system?

options.A: A separate legal entity for financial accounting purposes
options.B: A unit with legal responsibility for purchasing transactions
options.C: An area within a facility where materials are stored
options.D: A facility where a company executes some or all of its operations, such as a manufacturing, maintenance or storage facility

questions.explanation: A plant is key for processes that create or store materials.

questions.question: Which of the following tasks is completed at the plant level?

options.A: Negotiating terms and conditions with vendors
options.B: Material requirements planning, maintaining material stocks and executing production
options.C: Defining the chart of accounts of the enterprise
options.D: Closing posting periods

questions.explanation: Maintenance and service are also planned and executed at the plant level.

questions.question: Which parameter of a plant identifies the organization's working days and holidays?

options.A: Fiscal year variant
options.B: Posting period variant
options.C: Factory calendar
options.D: Holiday key

questions.explanation: When scheduling deliveries or payment dates, the system includes only working days.

questions.question: How is the factory calendar of GBI defined?

options.A: All days of the week are workdays with no holiday calendar attached (365 working days)
options.B: Only Monday to Friday are workdays
options.C: Only U.S. public holidays are excluded
options.D: Each plant has its own calendar at the plant level

questions.explanation: This lets GBI schedule activities for any day of the year.

questions.question: At which level are factory calendars and holiday calendars defined?

options.A: The plant level only
options.B: The company code level only
options.C: The client level, so they can be used by all company codes
options.D: The purchasing organization level

questions.explanation: GBI's plants are assigned to the US factory calendar.

questions.question: What is the relationship between a plant and a company code?

options.A: A plant belongs to only one company code, while a company code can have multiple plants
options.B: A plant can belong to several company codes, and a company code has only one plant
options.C: A plant and a company code have a one-to-one relationship
options.D: Plants are not assigned to company codes

questions.explanation: GBI's U.S. company has three plants and the German company two.

questions.question: What does the material valuation level specify?

options.A: The level at which materials are purchased from vendors
options.B: The enterprise structure level at which material prices and valuation of materials are established
options.C: The level at which storage conditions are defined
options.D: The level at which invoices are verified

questions.explanation: The two options are plant and company code.

questions.question: Which valuation level must be chosen to use production planning or product costing capabilities?

options.A: Company code level
options.B: Client level
options.C: Purchasing organization level
options.D: Plant level

questions.explanation: These techniques are plant specific. GBI elected plant-level valuation for this reason.

questions.question: What is true about the material valuation level once chosen?

options.A: It cannot be modified, must be defined before plants are assigned, and applies to all company codes in the client
options.B: It can be changed at any time for each company code
options.C: It is defined separately for each plant after it is created
options.D: It must be defined after the plants are assigned to company codes

questions.explanation: It is configured at the client level.

questions.question: With company code-level valuation, how is the price of a material treated across plants?

options.A: A material can have a different price in each plant
options.B: A material has no price in the plants
options.C: A material has the same price across all plants within the company code
options.D: Each purchasing organization sets its own price

questions.explanation: With plant-level valuation the same material can have different prices in different plants.

questions.question: What is a purchasing organization?

options.A: A unit with legal responsibility for all purchasing transactions involving vendors, including negotiating terms and resolving disputes
options.B: An individual or group who perform day-to-day purchasing activities
options.C: An area within a plant where materials are stored
options.D: A facility where operations are executed

questions.explanation: Only the purchasing organization has legal authority to enter into procurement transactions.

questions.question: In the plant-specific model of purchasing, how are purchasing organizations set up?

options.A: One purchasing organization is assigned to all plants of all company codes
options.B: One purchasing organization is assigned to a company code and all its plants
options.C: One purchasing organization is created for each plant and assigned to that plant and its company code
options.D: Purchasing organizations are not assigned to plants

questions.explanation: This is the most decentralized model.

questions.question: In the cross-plant model of purchasing, a purchasing organization is responsible for:

options.A: Procurement for all plants of all company codes
options.B: Procurement for all plants of one company code
options.C: Procurement for a single plant
options.D: Procurement for a single material group

questions.explanation: It is assigned to one company code and to all plants that belong to that company code.

questions.question: In the enterprise-level model, why is the purchasing organization NOT assigned to a company code?

options.A: Because it can only be assigned to plants, never to company codes
options.B: Because company codes do not exist at the enterprise level
options.C: Because it is assigned to the controlling area instead
options.D: Because its plants belong to more than one company code; the company code is identified when the purchase order is created

questions.explanation: This model standardizes procurement and exploits economies of scale.

questions.question: Which purchasing model has GBI adopted?

options.A: Only the enterprise-level model with GL00
options.B: A hybrid model: a central purchasing organization (GL00) plus country-specific purchasing organizations (US00, DE00)
options.C: Only a plant-specific model with one purchasing organization per plant
options.D: Only the cross-plant model with US00 and DE00

questions.explanation: GL00 negotiates contracts for the enterprise; US00 and DE00 take advantage of local customs.

questions.question: What does a purchasing group represent?

options.A: A unit with legal authority to enter into procurement transactions
options.B: A facility where materials are stored
options.C: A grouping of plants that share the same valuation
options.D: An individual or group of people who perform day-to-day purchasing activities for specific materials

questions.explanation: A purchasing group has no legal authority and serves multiple purchasing organizations.

questions.question: What is the key characteristic that distinguishes a purchasing group from a purchasing organization?

options.A: It is assigned to a company code
options.B: It negotiates enterprise-wide contracts
options.C: It does not have the legal authority to enter into procurement transactions
options.D: It is responsible for goods receipts

questions.explanation: GBI has purchasing groups E00 (Europe) and N00 (North America).

questions.question: What is a storage location?

options.A: An area within a plant where an organization stores materials
options.B: A facility where production is executed
options.C: A legal entity that holds the inventory accounts
options.D: A unit that negotiates with vendors

questions.explanation: GBI's storage locations differentiate raw materials, semifinished goods, finished products and trading goods.

questions.question: How many plants can a storage location be assigned to?

options.A: Several plants; a plant has exactly one storage location
options.B: Any number of plants and any number of locations
options.C: None; storage locations are assigned to company codes
options.D: Exactly one; a plant can have many storage locations

questions.explanation: Each storage location must be assigned to one and only one plant.

topics.topicName: Tax parameters, material types & price control

questions.question: What do tax-related parameters specify?

options.A: Whether a transaction is relevant for tax purposes and, if so, how to calculate the tax amounts
options.B: Which plants may purchase taxable materials
options.C: Which purchasing organization handles taxes
options.D: Which general ledger account receives the inventory posting

questions.explanation: Tax jurisdiction codes, tax versions and tax codes must be configured.

questions.question: What does the tax version define?

options.A: The tax rate of each tax jurisdiction
options.B: The default tax code of the company code
options.C: The number of tax codes and tax amounts available when entering a vendor invoice
options.D: The G/L account used for input tax

questions.explanation: Tax version 0801 allows one tax amount and code, 0802 two, and 0804 four.

questions.question: Which tax version allows up to four tax amounts and tax codes?
questions.explanation: GBI uses the version with one tax amount and one tax code for both company codes.

questions.question: What is a tax code?

options.A: A four-character key that identifies a company code
options.B: A ten-digit key that identifies a G/L account
options.C: A code identifying one of many U.S. tax authorities
options.D: A two-digit code assigned to the tax jurisdiction code that specifies the percent tax rate for different types of taxes

questions.explanation: Several tax codes are predefined, e.g., XI for input tax.

questions.question: What is input tax?

options.A: The tax collected by a company when it sells to customers
options.B: The tax paid by a company when it purchases materials from its vendors
options.C: The tax paid on the income of the company
options.D: The tax on payments to employees

questions.explanation: Output tax is collected when selling to customers.

questions.question: What do material types classify?

options.A: Materials based on the plant where they are stored
options.B: Materials based on the vendor that supplies them
options.C: Materials based on their weight and dimensions
options.D: Materials based on how the company utilizes them (purchased or made, used internally or sold)

questions.explanation: The use of a material determines which data are needed in its material master.

questions.question: How are material master data grouped?

options.A: By company codes
options.B: By user departments (views) based on functional areas such as purchasing, sales and accounting
options.C: By vendors
options.D: By posting periods

questions.explanation: Not all user departments are relevant for all material types.

questions.question: Which data are NOT relevant for finished products because they are produced in house?

options.A: Purchasing data
options.B: Accounting data
options.C: Sales data
options.D: Basic data

questions.explanation: Trading goods need purchasing data but not work-scheduling data.

questions.question: Which data are required for trading goods but not for finished products?

options.A: Work-scheduling data
options.B: Accounting data
options.C: Purchasing data
options.D: Basic data

questions.explanation: Trading goods are purchased and sold, but not produced.

questions.question: Which materials are valuated (stock) materials?

options.A: Materials for which both quantity and value are tracked, such as raw materials and trading goods
options.B: Materials whose value but not quantity is tracked
options.C: Materials expensed as supplies for which neither quantity nor value is tracked
options.D: Materials for which only the quantity is tracked

questions.explanation: The value is maintained in G/L accounts and the materials appear as assets on the balance sheet.

questions.question: What are non-stock materials?

options.A: Materials for which only the quantity is tracked
options.B: Materials produced in house but never sold
options.C: Materials treated as business expenses where neither quantity nor value is tracked, such as pens and notepads
options.D: Materials whose value is tracked but not their quantity

questions.explanation: Non-valuated materials track quantity but not value.

questions.question: What are non-valuated materials?

options.A: Materials for which the quantity is tracked but not the value
options.B: Materials for which the value is tracked but not the quantity
options.C: Materials for which neither quantity nor value is tracked
options.D: Materials for which both quantity and value are tracked

questions.explanation: For them quantity updating is enabled but value updating is not.

questions.question: What does the parameter price control determine?

options.A: Which general ledger account receives the inventory posting
options.B: Which tolerance limits apply to purchase orders
options.C: How the system calculates the cost (price) of a material: standard price or moving average price
options.D: Which plants may purchase the material

questions.explanation: Two options are available: standard price and moving average price (MAP).

questions.question: Which price control is typically used for purchased materials such as raw materials and trading goods?

options.A: Standard price
options.B: Moving average price (MAP)
options.C: No price control
options.D: Plant-level price control

questions.explanation: Materials produced in-house typically use standard price.

questions.question: Which price control is typically used for finished products and semifinished goods produced in house?

options.A: Moving average price
options.B: Weighted tax price
options.C: No price control
options.D: Standard price

questions.explanation: No price control is defined for non-valuated materials.

topics.topicName: Account determination: valuation class, account category reference & procedures

questions.question: When a goods receipt is recorded, which posting does the system make (e.g., 100 items x $75)?

options.A: A $7,500 debit to the vendor account and a credit to the inventory account
options.B: A $7,500 debit to the inventory account and a credit to the GR/IR account
options.C: A $7,500 debit to the GR/IR account and a credit to the bank account
options.D: A $7,500 debit to the price difference account and a credit to inventory

questions.explanation: When the invoice is received, the GR/IR account is cleared and the vendor account is credited.

questions.question: What happens at invoice verification in the basic scenario (no variances)?

options.A: The inventory account is credited and the bank account debited
options.B: The bank account is credited and the vendor account debited
options.C: The price difference account is debited
options.D: The GR/IR account is cleared and the vendor/A-P accounts are credited

questions.explanation: At payment the bank account is credited and the vendor account is cleared with a debit.

questions.question: Initial inventory is 200 items valued at $12,000. 100 more items are received at $75 each. What is the MAP after the goods receipt?
questions.explanation: The MAP before the receipt was $60; it is recalculated at goods receipt.

questions.question: With a vendor invoice of $8,500 including a $1,000 fuel surcharge and all 300 items still in inventory, what is the recalculated MAP?
questions.explanation: The $1,000 is posted to the inventory account and the material value increases.

questions.question: When is the moving average price recalculated?

options.A: At goods receipt and invoice receipt, not at goods issue
options.B: At goods issue only
options.C: At goods receipt and goods issue
options.D: At vendor payment only

questions.explanation: At goods issue the quantity and value are reduced but the MAP is unchanged.

questions.question: Materials are sold before the invoice with a $1,000 surcharge arrives. To which account is the $1,000 posted?

options.A: The inventory account
options.B: The GR/IR account
options.C: The price difference account (a temporary account)
options.D: The bank account

questions.explanation: Inventory cannot be credited because there is no inventory left.

questions.question: How is a tax amount on the invoice posted (e.g., $500 on $7,500)?

options.A: To an input tax account; it does not affect inventory valuation or the material master
options.B: To the inventory account, increasing the MAP
options.C: To the price difference account
options.D: To the GR/IR account

questions.explanation: All other accounts then have postings of $8,000 instead of $7,500.

questions.question: An invoice shows $7,502 instead of $7,500 because of a typographical error. Where is the $2 difference posted?

options.A: To the inventory account
options.B: To a temporary account (the price difference / small difference account)
options.C: To the bank account
options.D: To the tax account

questions.explanation: The company may also ask the vendor for a corrected invoice.

questions.question: From where does the system obtain the A/P reconciliation account in the procurement scenarios?

options.A: From the purchase order
options.B: From the material master
options.C: From the user at payment time
options.D: From the vendor master record

questions.explanation: The vendor subledger account comes from the purchase order; the bank account is entered by the user at payment.

questions.question: What is a valuation class?

options.A: A grouping of materials that have the same account determination (the same G/L account)
options.B: A grouping of plants with the same account determination rules
options.C: A link between valuation class and material type
options.D: A grouping of vendors with the same payment terms

questions.explanation: The valuation class is specified in the material master.

questions.question: What is the role of the account category reference?

options.A: It links the material type to the plant
options.B: It links the vendor to the purchasing organization
options.C: It links the valuation class and the material type
options.D: It links the posting key to the document type

questions.explanation: There is a one-to-many relationship between account category reference and valuation class.

questions.question: How is a valuation class related to an account category reference?

options.A: A valuation class can be assigned to only one account category reference
options.B: A valuation class can be assigned to several account category references
options.C: A valuation class is not related to account category references
options.D: A valuation class is assigned to a plant, not to an account category reference

questions.explanation: Likewise, a material type can be associated with only one account category reference.

questions.question: What does the valuation group code (grouping of valuation areas) allow?

options.A: Plants to be assigned to several company codes
options.B: Materials to be valued at the company code level
options.C: Account determination rules to be configured collectively for multiple plants that share the same rules
options.D: Vendors to share the same tolerance group

questions.explanation: The valuation modifier is the valuation group code.

questions.question: How many valuation grouping codes can a valuation area (plant) be assigned to?

options.A: Any number
options.B: Only one
options.C: Exactly two
options.D: None

questions.explanation: One code can be assigned to multiple plants and at least one code must be defined.

questions.question: If all plants of GBI use the same valuation group code, what must be true of the company codes?

options.A: They must use the same currency
options.B: They must have the same purchasing organization
options.C: They must be in the same country
options.D: They must use the same chart of accounts

questions.explanation: Otherwise separate rules are needed (e.g., one code for U.S. plants and another for German plants).

questions.question: Which account determination procedure (transaction) determines the inventory account?

options.A: WRX
options.B: BSX
options.C: DIF
options.D: ZDI

questions.explanation: The parameters are valuation modifier, valuation class and posting key.

questions.question: Which procedure (transaction) determines the GR/IR account?

options.A: BSX
options.B: DIF
options.C: PRD
options.D: WRX

questions.explanation: GBI uses one account (310000) for all materials regardless of valuation class.

questions.question: Which procedure (transaction) determines the small difference account?

options.A: BSX
options.B: WRX
options.C: DIF
options.D: ZDI

questions.explanation: It uses no valuation modifier or valuation class in GBI.

questions.question: Which procedure determines the G/L account for payment differences posted within tolerance on vendor payments?

options.A: ZDI
options.B: BSX
options.C: WRX
options.D: DIF

questions.explanation: It is similar to other account determination procedures.

questions.question: For an inventory posting, what does the posting key determine?

options.A: Which plant receives the posting
options.B: Which valuation class is used
options.C: Which tax code applies
options.D: Whether the posting is a debit (stock increase) or a credit (stock decrease)

questions.explanation: A debit is posted for an inward movement and a credit for an outward movement.

questions.question: Why is the price difference account for semifinished goods and finished products not the purchase price difference account?

options.A: Because they are always valued at moving average price
options.B: Because those materials are produced, not purchased; the production variance account is used
options.C: Because they have no valuation class
options.D: Because they are not stored in storage locations

questions.explanation: The production variance account is discussed in Chapter 6.

questions.question: What do tolerance limits tell the system?

options.A: How to proceed when data in a transaction deviate from the expected values
options.B: Which general ledger accounts to post to
options.C: Which materials are valuated materials
options.D: Which vendors may receive payments

questions.explanation: They are a form of financial control.

questions.question: What are the two options when a deviation exceeds the tolerance limit?

options.A: Warn and terminate, or error and continue
options.B: Block the vendor, or block the material
options.C: Warn and continue, or error and terminate
options.D: Reverse the document, or park the document

questions.explanation: With a warning the user can continue after acknowledging it; an error must be corrected.

questions.question: In which procurement steps can tolerance limits be specified?

options.A: Purchase order creation, goods receipt, invoice verification and vendor payment
options.B: Purchase requisition and purchase order only
options.C: Goods receipt and vendor payment only
options.D: Invoice verification only

questions.explanation: Tolerances can be percentages or amounts.

questions.question: Which tolerance key defines the purchase price tolerance?

options.A: SE
options.B: DQ
options.C: PP
options.D: PE

questions.explanation: The system compares the purchase order price with the valuation price in the material master.

questions.question: Which tolerance key determines the maximum permitted discount on a purchase order?

options.A: PE
options.B: SE
options.C: DW
options.D: VP

questions.explanation: Only percentage limits are available because the discount is expressed as a percent.

questions.question: The valuation price of a road helmet is $25 with upper limit 10% and lower limit 20%. A PO price of $27.60 will:

options.A: Be accepted without any message
options.B: Generate a warning (below $20)
options.C: Be blocked for payment
options.D: Generate a warning (above $27.50)

questions.explanation: Upper limit $27.50; lower limit $20; GBI is configured to warn and continue.

questions.question: What is an under delivery?

options.A: The quantity received is greater than the purchase order quantity
options.B: The quantity received is less than the purchase order quantity
options.C: The price invoiced is less than the PO price
options.D: The delivery arrives before the requested date

questions.explanation: The system typically permits under deliveries.

questions.question: If an under delivery exceeds tolerance at goods receipt, what does the system do?

options.A: Warns the user but completes the step and assumes a partial delivery
options.B: Displays an error and blocks the goods receipt
options.C: Blocks the invoice for payment
options.D: Closes the purchase order

questions.explanation: Additional deliveries can still be recorded unless the delivery complete indicator is set.

questions.question: What does the "delivery complete" indicator do?

options.A: It allows unlimited over deliveries
options.B: It blocks the invoice for payment
options.C: The system considers the purchase order complete and permits no additional deliveries
options.D: It sets the tolerance limit to 0%

questions.explanation: A user can set the indicator at any time, regardless of the quantity received.

questions.question: If over-delivered quantity exceeds the tolerance, what does the system do?

options.A: Displays an error and does not permit the user to complete the step
options.B: Displays a warning and completes the step
options.C: Completes the step without messages
options.D: Creates a new purchase order

questions.explanation: Within tolerance the system warns but lets the user continue.

questions.question: What does the "unlimited" over delivery option do?

options.A: It permits unlimited under deliveries
options.B: It disables the delivery complete indicator
options.C: It overrides the tolerance limit and permits unlimited over deliveries without any warnings
options.D: It permits invoices above the PO price

questions.explanation: It can be specified in the material master or the purchase order.

questions.question: Which tolerance keys address a change in the moving average price at goods receipt?

options.A: B1 (error and no PO creation) and B2 (warning but PO can be created)
options.B: PE and SE
options.C: DQ and DW
options.D: PP and VP

questions.explanation: They apply when the valuation price change exceeds the tolerance.

questions.question: In a two-way match, what is compared?

options.A: The invoice, goods receipt and purchase order data
options.B: The goods receipt and the payment
options.C: The invoice data with the purchase order data
options.D: The purchase requisition and the purchase order

questions.explanation: In a three-way match, quantities in all three documents and values in the PO and invoice must match.

questions.question: Which tolerance key is for quantity variance in a three-way match?

options.A: DW
options.B: DQ
options.C: PP
options.D: VP

questions.explanation: DW is for a two-way match where there is no goods receipt.

questions.question: What happens when an invoice variance exceeds the specified tolerance for DQ?

options.A: The system rejects the invoice and deletes it
options.B: The system pays the invoice immediately
options.C: The system posts the difference to the inventory account
options.D: The system records the invoice but adds a payment block

questions.explanation: A payment block prevents a user from paying the invoice.

questions.question: Which tolerance key compares the value of each invoice item with the PO item value (price variance)?

options.A: DQ
options.B: PP
options.C: DW
options.D: VP

questions.explanation: If the difference exceeds tolerance the invoice is blocked for payment.

questions.question: Which tolerance key relates to potential moving average price change when an invoice is recorded and results in only a warning (no payment block)?

options.A: PP
options.B: DQ
options.C: SE
options.D: VP

questions.explanation: Moving average price variance compares the new MAP to the previous one.

questions.question: What does a tolerance group for vendor payments specify?

options.A: Limits for purchase price differences defined as upper and lower limits
options.B: Limits for goods receipt quantity differences
options.C: Limits for permitted payment differences defined as gain or loss, in absolute amount or percentage
options.D: Limits for the amount an employee can post

questions.explanation: A gain is an underpayment of the invoice and a loss is an overpayment; the lower of absolute and percent limit applies.

questions.question: In a vendor payment tolerance group, what does a "gain" represent?

options.A: An underpayment of an invoice
options.B: An overpayment of an invoice
options.C: A discount granted by the vendor
options.D: A price increase in the purchase order

questions.explanation: A loss represents an overpayment.

questions.question: What does the plant parameter "create SLoc automatically" do?

options.A: Creates the plant automatically when a purchase order is created
options.B: Creates the material master automatically for new vendors
options.C: Creates storage location data for a material automatically when the first goods receipt is recorded
options.D: Creates storage locations for every plant at the same time

questions.explanation: Storage data for the plant must exist before materials can be stored there; for storage locations it is optional.

questions.question: Which master data are used when executing the procurement process steps?

options.A: Material master, vendor master and purchasing info records
options.B: Customer master, material master and routing
options.C: Cost elements, cost centers and activity types
options.D: G/L accounts, chart of accounts and posting keys

questions.explanation: The purchasing info record is not mandatory.

questions.question: At which level are the basic data of the material master (material number, description, weight, unit of measure) defined?

options.A: Plant level
options.B: Company code level
options.C: Client level
options.D: Purchasing organization level

questions.explanation: They are valid for all company codes in the enterprise.

questions.question: At which level are purchasing data in the material master defined?

options.A: Client level
options.B: Plant level
options.C: Company code level
options.D: Storage location level

questions.explanation: Purchasing data include purchasing group, under/over delivery tolerances and unlimited over delivery indicator.

questions.question: What do the storage data of the material master specify?

options.A: The valuation class and price control of the material
options.B: The purchasing group responsible for the material
options.C: The tolerance limits for goods receipts
options.D: Environmental conditions such as temperature and humidity required for storage, and shelf life

questions.explanation: They are defined for each plant and storage location.

questions.question: At which level are accounting data of the material master defined, and why?

options.A: Company code level, because all financial transactions impact the company code
options.B: Plant level, because material valuation is at the plant level
options.C: Client level, because they are general data
options.D: Storage location level, because stock is kept there

questions.explanation: In GBI, valuation is at plant level; there is no valuation at the storage location level.

questions.question: Which are key accounting data of the material master?

options.A: Purchasing group, payment terms and incoterms
options.B: Reconciliation account and tolerance group
options.C: Tax version, tax code and tax jurisdiction
options.D: Valuation class, price control, moving average price, quantity and value

questions.explanation: The valuation class links the material to the general ledger account.

questions.question: In the vendor master, at which level are general data, purchasing data and accounting data defined?

options.A: Plant level, company code level and client level respectively
options.B: Company code level, plant level and client level respectively
options.C: Client level, purchasing organization level and company code level respectively
options.D: Purchasing organization level for all three

questions.explanation: General data: number, name, address, tax data; purchasing data: currency, payment terms, incoterms.

questions.question: Which key accounting data in the vendor master are defined for each company code?

options.A: The reconciliation account number and the tolerance group for payments
options.B: The purchasing group and incoterms
options.C: The valuation class and price control
options.D: The tax version and tax code

questions.explanation: The reconciliation account determines the A/P account associated with the vendor.

questions.question: What is a purchasing info record?

options.A: A record containing data applicable to purchasing one specific material from one specific vendor
options.B: A record containing purchasing data valid for all vendors of a material
options.C: A record containing the purchasing data valid for all materials of a vendor
options.D: A record created automatically at every goods receipt

questions.explanation: It can be defined at the purchasing organization and plant levels.

questions.question: Which data are included in a purchasing info record but not in the material or vendor master?

options.A: Basic data such as weight and dimensions
options.B: Valuation class and price control
options.C: Typical and minimum order quantities, price conditions, and historical purchase order and quotation data
options.D: Reconciliation account and tolerance group

questions.explanation: Some data such as unit of measure and delivery tolerances also appear in the material or vendor master.

questions.question: Delivery tolerances exist in the material master, purchasing info record and purchase order. Which source does the system prefer?

options.A: The purchase order, followed by the info record, then the material master
options.B: The material master, followed by the info record, then the purchase order
options.C: The info record, followed by the material master, then the purchase order
options.D: The vendor master, then the material master

questions.explanation: The system prefers more specific data over general data.

questions.question: Is the purchasing info record mandatory master data for the procurement process?

options.A: Yes, no purchase order can be created without it
options.B: Yes, but only for trading goods
options.C: No, but it connects the material master and vendor master and records the vendor/material relationship
options.D: No, and it has no purpose

questions.explanation: It identifies which vendors a material was bought from and which materials were bought from a vendor.

questions.question: Which testing types are typically used for the procurement process?

options.A: Unit and performance testing only
options.B: Scenario, integration and user acceptance testing
options.C: Regression and modification testing
options.D: Only user acceptance testing

questions.explanation: Each process step must be tested: requisition, PO, goods receipt, invoice verification, vendor payment.

questions.question: What does testing of procurement confirm regarding automatic account determination?

options.A: That the MAP never changes
options.B: That no tolerance limits are needed
options.C: That the chart of accounts has only one account
options.D: That the procedures result in correct postings to the various accounts

questions.explanation: Testing also checks that business rules and parameters are executed properly.

topics.topicName: TS410 – Source to Pay process & S/4HANA changes

questions.question: Which is the correct order of the steps in the source-to-pay business process?

options.A: Purchase order, requirements determination, goods receipt, payment, invoice verification, PO monitoring, source determination
options.B: Source determination, goods receipt, purchase requisition, invoice verification, payment
options.C: Invoice verification, goods receipt, purchase order, requirements determination, payment
options.D: Requirements determination, source determination, purchase order, PO monitoring, goods receipt, invoice verification, payment

questions.explanation: Seven steps from requirement to payment of vendor liabilities.

questions.question: How can a purchase requisition be created automatically?

options.A: By the goods receipt posting
options.B: By Materials Requirements Planning (MRP), maintenance orders, production orders or networks
options.C: By the automatic payment run
options.D: By the invoice verification step

questions.explanation: It can also be created manually by the requesting department or initiated from SAP Ariba.

questions.question: How can the buyer find the supplier with the best price?

options.A: By posting a valuated goods receipt
options.B: By running the automatic payment program
options.C: By checking the stock overview report
options.D: By requesting quotations (RFQs) and comparing prices between supply sources or quotations

questions.explanation: Existing POs, outline agreements and info records are also supply sources.

questions.question: Why should a goods receipt be entered with reference to the purchase order?

options.A: It reduces entries, lets the system check material and quantity against the PO and updates the PO history
options.B: It automatically pays the vendor invoice
options.C: It creates the purchase requisition retroactively
options.D: It removes the need for a material document

questions.explanation: The system proposes all open PO items.

questions.question: What does Logistics Invoice Verification (LIV) do?

options.A: Pays the vendor and clears the open item on the vendor account
options.B: Posts the goods receipt against the purchase order
options.C: Enters vendor invoices and credit memos relating to a PO and completes the procurement process in MM, excluding payment
options.D: Creates the purchase requisition from the MRP run

questions.explanation: Posting the invoice updates the PO history and creates an open item on the vendor account.

questions.question: What happens to foreign trade functionality in SAP S/4HANA on-premise?

options.A: It is not available in MM; SAP Global Trade Services (GTS) is the successor
options.B: It remains part of standard MM unchanged
options.C: It is replaced by SAP Ariba
options.D: It is moved to Financial Accounting

questions.explanation: SAP GTS can be connected to SAP S/4HANA.

questions.question: From which table is the actual stock quantity calculated on the fly in SAP S/4HANA?

options.A: The table MARD
options.B: The table EKPO
options.C: The new material document table MATDOC
options.D: The table ACDOCA

questions.explanation: Having most information in one place gives simple and fast reporting.

questions.question: What is obligatory for material valuation in SAP S/4HANA?

options.A: Actual Costing
options.B: The statistical moving average price
options.C: Foreign Trade
options.D: The Material Ledger

questions.explanation: Actual Costing remains optional.

questions.question: What is the effect of deactivating the statistical moving average price?

options.A: It makes Actual Costing mandatory for all materials
options.B: Exclusive locks are no longer needed for standard price materials, so goods-movement throughput increases; it is not reversible
options.C: It can be reversed at any time by any user
options.D: It changes the financial valuation of all stock

questions.explanation: Materials with price control Moving Average are still limited by exclusive locking.

questions.question: What do the two price controls for a material mean?

options.A: Standard gives fixed-price valuation; Moving Average lets any transaction change unit costs
options.B: Standard changes with every goods movement; Moving Average is fixed
options.C: Both are fixed prices that only differ by currency
options.D: Standard is used for services; Moving Average for consumables only

questions.explanation: Standard price gives much higher throughput for goods movements.

questions.question: Which channels does the new SAP S/4HANA output management support?

options.A: Fax, telex and EDI only
options.B: Only SAP Script printing
options.C: E-mail, printout and XML
options.D: Only workflow events

questions.explanation: The new output management is based on BRF+ instead of NAST.

questions.question: What is SAP Ariba in the intelligent-spend scenario?

options.A: The connection to the business network, a collaboration platform where partners exchange information
options.B: The digital core that stores all transactions
options.C: The planning extension for S&OP
options.D: The tool for creating forms and logos

questions.explanation: The digital core is S/4HANA; IBP is the planning extension.

questions.question: What is the client?

options.A: The smallest unit with a complete set of books, identified by a four-character key
options.B: The highest organizational unit, self-contained legally, organizationally and in data, identified by a three-digit key
options.C: A unit that subdivides the enterprise by purchasing requirements
options.D: A unit that differentiates stocks of material within a plant

questions.explanation: Data created at client level applies to all company codes.

questions.question: How is a company code defined in a client?

options.A: By a three-digit numeric key
options.B: By a two-character key
options.C: By the plant it belongs to
options.D: By a four-character alphanumeric key

questions.explanation: Several company codes can be set up in one client.

questions.question: What is the role of the purchasing organization?

options.A: It represents a buyer who contacts vendors
options.B: It procures materials or services and negotiates purchase conditions with vendors
options.C: It keeps stocks of material in a plant
options.D: It produces the balance sheet of the company

questions.explanation: It subdivides the enterprise by purchasing requirements.

questions.question: What is a plant?

options.A: A logistics unit that subdivides the enterprise into production, procurement and materials planning
options.B: A unit of external accounting with its own balance sheet
options.C: A group of buyers responsible for purchasing
options.D: A key identifying the storage bin

questions.explanation: It can represent a production facility, a regional sales office or a maintenance location.

questions.question: What is the relationship between plants and company codes?

options.A: A plant can belong to several company codes
options.B: A company code can contain only one plant
options.C: A company code may contain several plants, but a plant can belong to only one company code
options.D: Plants and company codes are not related

questions.explanation: Specifying the plant therefore also specifies the company code.

questions.question: How are storage locations assigned to plants?

options.A: Several storage locations can belong to one plant, but a storage location belongs to only one plant
options.B: One storage location can belong to several plants
options.C: Each plant has exactly one storage location
options.D: Storage locations are assigned to company codes directly

questions.explanation: The same storage location key can be reused in different plants.

questions.question: At which level is inventory management carried out?

options.A: At the client level
options.B: At the storage location level within the plant
options.C: At the purchasing group level
options.D: At the company code level

questions.explanation: Storage locations differentiate stocks of materials in a plant.

questions.question: How is a cross-company-code purchasing organization set up?

options.A: By assigning it to every plant
options.B: By assigning it to one company code only
options.C: By assigning it to a storage location
options.D: By not assigning the purchasing organization to any company code

questions.explanation: The system asks for the company code when a PO is created.

questions.question: What characterizes a plant-specific purchasing organization?

options.A: It procures for all plants in the client
options.B: It is assigned to one company code and one plant and procures materials for that plant only
options.C: It is not assigned to any company code
options.D: It is assigned to several company codes

questions.explanation: A cross-plant purchasing organization is assigned to a company code and procures for its plants.

topics.topicName: TS410 – Material, vendor & info record master data

questions.question: Why is all material data stored in one material master record?

options.A: To eliminate data redundancy so purchasing, inventory management, planning and invoice verification use the same data
options.B: To limit access to a single department
options.C: To prevent changes after the material is created
options.D: To avoid change documents for the material

questions.explanation: Each department works with its own view of the record.

questions.question: Which data is stored at the client level of the material master?

options.A: The storage bin and picking data
options.B: The purchasing group and price control
options.C: Data valid for all plants, such as the base unit of measure, goods group and short text
options.D: The warehouse number and storage type

questions.explanation: The purchase order text is also maintained at client level.

questions.question: Which data is typically stored at plant level in the material master?

options.A: Purchasing group, purchase order unit of measure, shelf-life data and price control
options.B: Base unit of measure and the material short text
options.C: The storage bin of the material
options.D: The vendor address and bank details

questions.explanation: Much purchasing, inventory and valuation data is kept at plant level.

questions.question: Which data is stored at the storage location level?

options.A: The purchase order text
options.B: The base unit of measure
options.C: The price control of the material
options.D: Data valid for a particular storage location, such as the storage bin

questions.explanation: Client, plant and storage location matter for external procurement.

questions.question: What is the difference between creating and changing a material in the transactions?

options.A: Change can add new views; Create can only display data
options.B: Create extends a material by adding missing views or levels; Change can only modify views and levels that already exist
options.C: Both can add views and levels without limits
options.D: Create deletes the existing change documents

questions.explanation: All changes are logged in change documents.

questions.question: Which transaction is the single point of entry for business partners, customers and vendors in S/4HANA?

options.A: Transaction ME21N
options.B: Transaction MIGO
options.C: Transaction MIRO
options.D: Transaction BP

questions.explanation: It can also be maintained through a Fiori app.

questions.question: Which statement about the business partner category is true?

options.A: It can be changed at any time
options.B: It determines the fields available for entry and cannot be changed after the partner is created
options.C: It defines the purchasing organization
options.D: It defines the number of company codes

questions.explanation: The categories are person, organization and group.

questions.question: At which level is the data of the FI Vendor role maintained?

options.A: At the company code level
options.B: At the client level
options.C: At the purchasing organization level
options.D: At the plant level

questions.explanation: It contains the reconciliation account and payment methods.

questions.question: Where is the purchasing data of a supplier maintained?

options.A: In the FI Vendor role for each company code
options.B: In the general role for each client
options.C: In the Supplier role for each purchasing organization
options.D: In the material master for each plant

questions.explanation: It includes PO currency, Incoterms and partner roles.

questions.question: Which information does a purchasing info record store?

options.A: The stock quantities of a material per storage location
options.B: Vendor-material information such as prices and conditions, delivery data, vendor data and the last PO number
options.C: The G/L accounts used for goods receipts
options.D: The payment run settings of the vendor

questions.explanation: It is stored at purchasing organization and plant level.

questions.question: How do the two text types in an info record differ?

options.A: The memo is printed; the PO text is internal only
options.B: Both texts are printed on the PO
options.C: Neither is transferred to the PO item
options.D: The internal memo is not printed; the PO text describes the PO item and is printed

questions.explanation: Both can be transferred to the PO item.

questions.question: Where do conditions of a contract apply?

options.A: To all POs of the vendor
options.B: To all contract release orders created with reference to the contract
options.C: Only to the info record of one material
options.D: Only to the goods receipt

questions.explanation: Info record conditions apply to PO items with that material and vendor.

topics.topicName: TS410 – Purchase requisitions, purchase orders & account assignment

questions.question: Who determines the source of supply for a purchase requisition?

options.A: The purchasing department, which assigns a source and then converts the requisition into a PO or RFQ
options.B: The requesting department only
options.C: The accounting department when the invoice arrives
options.D: The warehouse after the goods receipt

questions.explanation: The source determination can be automated.

questions.question: When must an account assignment be entered for a PO item?

options.A: For all stock materials
options.B: Only for materials with moving average price
options.C: For pure consumables, materials without a master record and services
options.D: Only for items from info records

questions.explanation: Stock materials take the account assignment from the material master valuation class.

questions.question: What does account assignment category K stand for?

options.A: An asset, with the asset number
options.B: A cost center, together with a G/L consumption account
options.C: A sales order
options.D: A project network

questions.explanation: Category A is the asset.

questions.question: How is the G/L account determined for account assignment category A?

options.A: Manually from the cost center
options.B: From the purchasing group
options.C: From the vendor master record
options.D: Automatically from the asset number; it cannot be entered manually

questions.explanation: The asset number must be entered on the account assignment screen.

questions.question: What do stock materials need for procurement?

options.A: An account assignment category and cost center
options.B: A material master record; no account assignment category is given in the PO
options.C: No master record and only a short text
options.D: A purchase requisition from SAP Ariba

questions.explanation: The goods receipt posts to a stock account based on the valuation class.

questions.question: What must be entered manually when procuring a consumable without a material master?

options.A: The valuation class and price control
options.B: The storage location and storage bin
options.C: The vendor bank details
options.D: A short description, a material group and a purchase order unit

questions.explanation: This data cannot be fetched from a master record.

questions.question: What happens when a purchase requisition for a consumable on a cost object is saved?

options.A: The vendor is paid automatically
options.B: A material document is created
options.C: A commitment is created in Management Accounting if commitment management is activated
options.D: The stock value of the material increases

questions.explanation: The same happens when the PO is saved.

questions.question: Which data is in the header of a purchase order?

options.A: Material, quantity, delivery date and price
options.B: Document type, supplier, purchasing organization, purchasing group, company code, currency and payment terms
options.C: Storage location and storage bin
options.D: Material group and valuation class

questions.explanation: Items hold material, quantity, price, delivery date and plant.

questions.question: What does the item category of a PO item determine?

options.A: The company code of the PO
options.B: The payment terms of the vendor
options.C: The currency of the invoice
options.D: The procurement process for the item, e.g., consignment, subcontracting or stock transfer

questions.explanation: A standard PO is used for external suppliers.

questions.question: Which type of order is used when the source of supply is a plant of your own company?

options.A: A standard purchase order
options.B: A stock transport order
options.C: A consignment order
options.D: A purchase requisition

questions.explanation: Standard POs go to external suppliers.

questions.question: Which data does the system propose when entering a PO?

options.A: The goods receipt quantity and storage location
options.B: The invoice number and the bank account
options.C: The cost center and the profit center
options.D: Ordering address, payment terms and Incoterms from the vendor; material text and group from the material master; price from an info record

questions.explanation: Defaults reduce the entries needed.

topics.topicName: TS410 – Goods receipt, invoice verification & payment

questions.question: Which movement type is used to post a goods receipt for a PO to valuated stock?

options.A: Movement type 102
options.B: Movement type 201
options.C: Movement type 301
options.D: Movement type 101

questions.explanation: Each movement type has a cancellation type, usually the number + 1.

questions.question: Into which stock types can a goods receipt be posted?

options.A: Only unrestricted-use stock
options.B: Unrestricted-use, quality inspection and blocked stock
options.C: Only blocked and consignment stock
options.D: Only quality inspection stock

questions.explanation: Withdrawals for consumption are possible only from unrestricted-use stock.

questions.question: What does the movement type control?

options.A: Only the print output of the GR slip
options.B: Only the vendor payment terms
options.C: Only the PO currency
options.D: The way goods are moved, the screen layout and the automatic account determination

questions.explanation: It is a three-character key.

questions.question: What does posting a goods movement create?

options.A: A material document and, if valuation-relevant, an accounting document
options.B: A purchase requisition and a quotation
options.C: A vendor invoice and a payment document
options.D: A cost center and a profit center

questions.explanation: Both documents are created simultaneously and are independent.

questions.question: How can an incorrect material document be corrected?

options.A: By changing the quantity in the document
options.B: By changing the movement type
options.C: By canceling it and creating a new document, since quantities, material and movement type cannot be changed
options.D: By deleting the document from the database

questions.explanation: Documents of goods movements are immutable.

questions.question: How is the accounting document of a goods movement uniquely identified?

options.A: By company code, accounting document number and fiscal year
options.B: By plant and storage location
options.C: By material and movement type
options.D: By purchasing group and vendor

questions.explanation: The company code is determined from the plant.

questions.question: Which goods movement does not result in any FI posting?

options.A: A goods receipt of raw material
options.B: A goods receipt of a consumable
options.C: A transfer of raw material within one plant
options.D: A scrapping of a valuated material

questions.explanation: Only valuation-relevant movements create accounting documents.

questions.question: What is updated by a goods receipt of a stock material?

options.A: The vendor open item
options.B: The output tax account
options.C: The payment run proposal list
options.D: On-hand stock quantity, the PO history and, via the Material Ledger, the moving average price

questions.explanation: Quality management may also create an inspection lot.

questions.question: What does a GR of a consumable additionally create?

options.A: A stock transport order
options.B: A controlling document in Management Accounting, clearing the commitment and posting actual costs
options.C: A bank statement
options.D: A new purchase info record

questions.explanation: FI and Material Ledger documents are created as well.

questions.question: What does the invoice verification propose when entering an invoice with PO reference?

options.A: All items of the PO, regardless of earlier invoices
options.B: Items not yet fully invoiced and the expected value, the quantity still to be invoiced times the order price
options.C: Only the payment terms of the vendor
options.D: The goods receipt quantity as the invoiced value

questions.explanation: If 100 were delivered and 60 invoiced, 40 pieces remain.

questions.question: What happens when the invoice deviates from the PO beyond tolerances?

options.A: The system posts the invoice and pays it immediately
options.B: The system deletes the PO
options.C: The system reverses the goods receipt
options.D: The system blocks the invoice for payment

questions.explanation: Price and quantity differences trigger tolerance checks.

questions.question: What are effects of posting a supplier invoice?

options.A: Stock quantities increase and a material document is created
options.B: An accounting document is created, the GR/IR account is cleared, the PO history is updated and an open vendor item is posted
options.C: The vendor is paid and the open item is cleared
options.D: The purchase requisition is converted into a PO

questions.explanation: The output tax account is also updated.

questions.question: How are payment media created by the automatic payment program in S/4HANA?

options.A: By the Materials Requirements Planning run
options.B: By the goods receipt transaction
options.C: By the document splitting function
options.D: By the Payment Medium Workbench (PMW), e.g., printed cheques, IDocs for EDI or DME data files

questions.explanation: Vendors can also be paid manually.
